findings.reason: as written the builder must either satisfy §13's exclusion or §16's marker read, and it cannot do both; implementing the marker read as written reopens the concurrent-launch window §13 closed.
findings.text: §16 says "With only the marker, the key reads the dispatched attempt the marker carries", and "the marker" is `attempt.json`: `dispatch.py:2772` writes it as `_supervisor_write(directory / ATTEMPT_RECORD_NAME, ...)` and `ATTEMPT_RECORD_NAME = "attempt.json"` (`dispatch_launch.py:1940`), the same file §16 itself calls "The attempt marker near line 2772". §13's own constraint list — which §16 says "the design must meet all of them" — states the opposite: "The in-flight `attempt.json` is excluded from the key, so two racing doors compute the same key even after the first has written it, and the held reservation refuses the second." The current implementation does exclude it: `launch_reservation_key` (`dispatch_launch.py:2218`) reads only `attempt_receipt_numbers` plus the canonical `worker.json`/`exit.json` by the attempt they carry, never `attempt.json`. Reading the marker back into the key restores the divergence for a run with no receipts: the dispatch door writes its marker at line 2772 and reserves at line 2862, so a second door that reads the key inside that ~90-line span sees no marker and keys on 1 while the first keys on the dispatched attempt, and both admissions succeed — the two-workers-in-one-worktree outcome the whole plan exists to prevent. The section's own regression measure ("the two-door first-attempt cases ... each refuse the second door at both base and head") will not catch it, because §13's existing case drives the two doors in sequence, never interleaved across that span.

findings.reason: it splits §16 into a behaviour node and a test-repair node, each with a verdict and a gate that can actually show its own change.
findings.text: §16 bundles two distinct deliverables: the reservation repairs (the paired shadow arm's attempt, the solo-shadow marker, the suppressed supervisor rewrite, and the dead `claim_next_attempt`/`release_attempt_claim` pair) and a separate test-quality deliverable raised by a code-health review — merging the duplicated `_create_attempt_claim` fixture in `tests/test_staged_write_inventory.py`, replacing the vacuous `assert pid > 0` at `tests/test_a_concurrent_launch_is_refused.py:446` and `:466`, strengthening the fresh-run case at `:776`, and renaming `test_a_fresh_run_id_takes_no_reservation`. A single verdict on §16 cannot close the test repairs without also passing the behaviour changes, and the mechanical deletion cannot be judged apart from them; the repository's own commit rule keeps mechanical removals in their own commit. The four behaviours do all resolve to one mechanism, so splitting the test-quality work is the whole change.

findings.reason: both sections are landed and every named function (`_launcher_refusal`, `_stream_reading_refusal`, `_create_worktree`, `_prepare_attempt_records`) resolves, so the drift costs a reader a search rather than sending a builder to wrong code.
findings.text: §6 locates the three refusal sites as "`reckon/crew/resumption.py` near lines 1001 and 1112, and `reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py` near line 1223", but those lines now land in unrelated code: the two resumption sites are `_launcher_refusal` at `resumption.py:1266` and `_stream_reading_refusal` at `resumption.py:1369`, roughly 265 lines further down, and §10's "`dispatch.py` creates the worktree first, near line 2773" is likewise `_create_worktree` at `dispatch.py:2892`, and its "`_prepare_attempt_records` near line 1958" is at `dispatch_launch.py:2472`. A reader following the line pointer finds nothing to read; the symbol names in the surrounding prose are the only resolvable part.

response_events.note: §16 now reconciles with §13: the key reads the marker's attempt as it stands, never plus one, so two doors racing on a first attempt still compute one key and the held reservation refuses the second. §13's constraint exists to keep racing doors on one key, and this keeps it; §16 states that it narrows §13's exclusion to the plus-one case.

rubric_items.done_when: pass — every node names a declared negative control and a measurable case; the mutation is named against a case it reddens in §4–§13 and §16, and the two sections without an explicit mutation (§15, and §14) declare a base-arm comparison with the new test copied into the base tree.
